mechanism: Test whether query appearance parts support one shared translation/rotation/isotropic-scale transform, optionally mirrored, of the reference object. Two landmarks propose a pose; other landmarks validate it. Accepted poses transfer the entire reference mask into a complete query prior.
inputs: same existing frozen MEAN continuous field64
input_exposure: No query GT, class/fold IDs, extra model or encoder invocation; actual cohort bindings not yet made
steps: Compress pure-reference foreground features into up to eight deterministic spherical modes, and define each landmark by its coverage-weighted spatial centroid.
Require at least four modes; fewer modes do not support held-out geometric validation and retain the base.

Compute each query token's cosine to every mode. The mode-specific response is cosine-to-this-mode minus the strongest competing-mode cosine; common equal responses to all modes supply no part arrangement evidence.
Per mode center these margins by the query median, divide by max(1.4826*MAD,0.01), clip to [-3,3]; keep eight spatially separated mode-response peaks with radius3 tokens.
Enumerate poses from every landmark pair and their query peak pairs, with direct and mirrored reference coordinates; keep scale in [0.125,8] and reference pair distance>=1 token.

Bilinearly sample all mode-specific standardized responses at predicted query landmark positions. Both generating landmarks must score>=1.5. At least ceil(0.75*(K-2)) held-out landmarks must also score>=1.5, and both held-out mean and whole mean must reach1.5.

Sort by held-out consensus, remove duplicate poses and masks overlapping earlier accepted masks at IoU>=0.5, with no explicit cap on retained instances. Inverse-warp the full reference coverage; take the pointwise maximum of all accepted mask priors.
If no pose passes, keep the base. Otherwise output 0.5*clipped-base+0.5*aligned-mask-prior for every query token, then bilinear1024 and threshold>0.5.

Save original/clipped base, same-mode bag-response fusion without pose geometry, and aligned-prior-only controls. Controls and internal poses do not count as additional methods. Seal predictions before query-GT scoring.

prediction.conditional: If same-class objects preserve the relative positions of distinguishable reference appearance parts more consistently than confusing regions, held-out pose agreement can distinguish them even when individual part-match strengths are equal.
proved_or_structurally_checked: Equal per-part similarity does not imply equal spatial-pose consensus
Fitting two peaks alone cannot pass the held-out-landmark criterion
Uniform equal cosine responses to all reference modes do not constitute distinct part evidence
Repeated identical poses do not change the prior
Inverse similarity-transform mask transfer matches the specified translation/rotation mapping
Reference-mode count below four and absence of a valid pose retain the base
not_claimed: semantic identity guaranteed by a rigid pose

counterexamples: Articulation, viewpoint changes and nonrigid deformation may destroy the single-similarity-transform model for the true class.
A wrong category can share the same distinguishable part layout and pass consensus.
Reference feature modes can have unstable or colocated centroids rather than genuine anatomical/object parts.
Query parts absent from the top-eight spatial peak lists cannot propose their true pose; this can miss additional same-class instances.
Too few pure foreground tokens/modes or occluded parts can cause abstention.
Transferred reference silhouette can differ from the true query shape; globally blending the union prior may delete unmatched correct instances or add warped background.
The finite pose search selects among many dependent hypotheses; the consensus threshold is not a calibrated probability or a statistical significance claim.

cpu_cost.mask_nms: Worst case O(A^2*N); accepted-pose count and actual time must be reported, no complete-cohort minute guarantee

simple_alternative: Use the same mode-specific response bank in a bag fusion without geometric constraints; the pose method must add value beyond that same-information control.
